Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. The sun is out, but dark clouds have started to gather around the ground once again. Let's hope they pass by without causing any further interruptions. It will be the left-hand, right-hand opening combination of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma for India. Lauren Filer will kick things off with the new ball. Nat Sciver-Brunt has not taken the field. In her absence, Charlie Dean will be the acting skipper. Alice Capsey has donned the gloves instead of Amy Jones. Mandhana to face the first ball. Away we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

India let momentum slip at the death - It was a mixed outing with the ball for India Women. Renuka Singh Thakur struck early with the new ball, but chances were few and the ground fielding left a bit to be desired. Shafali Verma's golden arm broke a crucial stand, while Radha Yadav and Sree Charani chipped in with a wicket each. Shreyanka Patil was the pick of the bowlers with 2/29, but England's late charge, including 19 runs off Renuka's final over, shifted the momentum and left India's batters with a challenging chase ahead. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Hosts recover smartly after early stumble - England Women were far from their fluent best in the Powerplay, losing Danni Wyatt-Hodge early and crawling to just 39/1 after six overs. Amy Jones then injected momentum with a classy 64 off 45, sharing a 70-run stand with Nat Sciver-Brunt. The skipper struggled to get going and even survived a lucky escape when a potential catch off her boot went unreviewed due to the absence of DRS. Rain halted play for just over an hour with Sciver-Brunt on 30 off 30, but she returned looking far more assured, finishing with a well-made 57 off 45. A late burst from Danielle Gibson, smashing 30 off just 12, then lifted England past the 170-run mark.

England end on a high with an explosive finish - England Women finished with a flourish, smashing 43 runs off the final three overs to post a strong total and seize the momentum heading into the break. India Women had their moments with the ball and kept the scoring in check for large periods, but their death-bowling woes resurfaced at the worst possible time. Whether the target proves enough remains to be seen, but England will head into the break feeling they have enough on the board.
Back of a length, outside off, Danielle Gibson looks to slap it but gets it off the toe end. The ball rolls towards cover as the batters collect a single. England Women end their innings at 171/6.

Update 10.47 am GMT (4.17 pm IST) - It has brightened up considerably, with blue skies now visible above the ground. The two umpires have made their way over to the Indian camp and are relaying their observations to the head coach, Amol Muzumdar and the captain, Harmanpreet Kaur. And there you go, we have a resumption time. Play to resume at 11.05 am GMT (4.35 pm IST). No word yet on the revised conditions, if any, but we shall have that update soon.

Update 10.38 am GMT (4.08 pm IST) - It did seem like a bit of drizzle was still lingering around the ground as the clean-up operation was briefly halted, but the ground staff are back at work now. Well, the sun is out and so are the match officials, who have made their way onto the field to have a look at the conditions. They are currently in conversation with one of the members of the ground staff, possibly discussing the turnaround time required to get the ground ready.

Update 10.24 am GMT (3.54 pm IST) - Good news! The rain has eased. The groundsmen are slowly taking the covers off. We can see a few puddles of water on the covers, which explains the cautious approach, but the clean-up operation is well underway. Stay tuned.

Update 10 am GMT (3.30 pm IST) - Oh no! The drizzle has picked up. The groundsmen get the hover cover on. They clearly feel this could be more than just a passing shower, which is why the square and the run-up areas are also being covered. Let's hope it goes away soon and the play resumes. Stick around for regular updates.

Commentary.Commentary: Right then, we are all set for the action to begin. There was a slight scare of the drizzle earlier, but it has cleared now, and it is getting brighter. The two umpires and the players make their way out in the middle. Amy Jones and Danni Wyatt-Hodge open up for England Women. Spin straightaway as Shafali Verma starts with the new ball. Let's go...

PITCH REPORT - Tash Farrant is down by the pitch and notes that there is a nice, light breeze blowing across the ground. Informs that the match will be played on the same surface that was used for the warm-up games on Monday. She points out that the wicket is a touch dry but still feels rock solid underneath. Farrant reckons the spinners could have a big role to play through the middle overs. She also highlights the big pockets of the ground, which means batters will need to run hard between the wickets. Feels it will be important for teams to make the most of the Powerplay while the ball is hard.

The skipper of England Women - Nat Sciver-Brunt says that she wanted to bowl as well. She adds that she would like some time in the middle with the bat, and they will try to adapt to the conditions. She does not remember the changes, but there are a few for this game.

The captain of India Women - Harmanpreet Kaur says that this game is the right opportunity to test themselves as she thinks chasing will be hard. Adds that the way they played in the last game was excellent with bat, ball and in the field. Informs that Deepti, Arundhati, and Nandni are resting.

India want to finalise their ideal playing eleven before facing Pakistan, while England aim to regain ultimate confidence before tackling Sri Lanka. England's strategy check - England will be looking to bounce back and find their rhythm after a recent loss to Australia. The team is currently experimenting with a revamped top order, promoting Amy Jones to open and slotting captain Nat Sciver-Brunt in at number three. While their lower-middle order has shown great fighting spirit, England's bowling unit will be eager to step up and show more depth beyond Sophie Ecclestone today.

A peek into World Cup plans - The ICC Women's T20 World Cup is just days away, and at Sophia Gardens in Cardiff, two of the tournament's heavyweights will face off in their final warm-up fixture before the real business begins. India Women and England Women, both coming off contrasting warm-up results will use this opportunity to fine-tune combinations, test bench strength, and walk onto the World Cup stage with clarity in their plans. For India, this is a chance to build on a winning start. For England, it's about bouncing back and finding rhythm before their tournament opener against Sri Lanka. Fulmali stakes her claim - India entered this warm-up campaign on the back of a narrow 2-1 series defeat to England, a result that left Harmanpreet Kaur's side with several points to ponder ahead of the World Cup. While the scoreline was tight, the loss exposed familiar vulnerabilities, particularly an over-reliance on the top order and a lack of death-over firepower. The good news from their first warm-up is that the opening pair of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma looks to have regained its aggressive mojo, racing to 59 in just 5.1 overs against the West Indies. Then came the middle-order rescue act. Bharti Fulmali, one of the players Harmanpreet specifically wanted to give game time, made a compelling case with an unbeaten 56 off 40 balls, anchoring the innings after a mid-overs wobble. Finishing issues still haunt India - The concern, however, remains the middle-order fragility. From 146/4 to 162/7, India lost three wickets in just 16 runs, a reminder that beyond their top order and Fulmali, the finishing department remains a work in progress. Richa Ghosh fell for a golden duck, and the lower order struggled to capitalize on the platform laid by the openers and Fulmali. Spin dominance - Where India looked truly formidable was with the ball, specifically, their spin attack. Shreyanka Patil (4/36) and Radha Yadav (3/25) dismantled the West Indies' chase, triggering a collapse from 63/1 to 113/7 in a matter of overs. With Deepti Sharma waiting in the wings and Sree Charani also in the squad, India's spin arsenal looks deep enough to trouble any batting lineup in helpful conditions. The pace attack, however, remains a question mark, especially with Renuka Singh Thakur's fitness uncertain and the seamers struggling for consistency in the recent series against England. Top-order experiments - England entered their warm-up against Australia with a revamped batting order. Sophia Dunkley, who managed just 98 runs across six innings in the preceding series against New Zealand and India, was dropped with wicketkeeper Amy Jones promoted to open alongside Danni Wyatt-Hodge. Captain Nat Sciver-Brunt, playing her first international match of the summer, slotted in at No. 3 as a specialist batter as she continues her recovery from a calf injury. Middle-order resistance - The experiment, however, did not yield immediate dividends. Jones and Wyatt-Hodge fell cheaply, and Sciver-Brunt managed just 3 before being cleaned up. But the middle order showed fight. Alice Capsey anchored the innings with 45 off 36, Freya Kemp provided a late surge, and Dani Gibson remained unbeaten on 27 off 16 to push England to fighting score. On another day, against a less formidable attack, that total might have been enough. Need more from the bowlers - The defeat raises questions about England's bowling attack beyond Sophie Ecclestone. Lauren Bell and Lauren Filer showed glimpses, but against the best batting units, England may need more wickets from their spinners in the middle overs. The batting, however, looks better placed with Capsey's form, Kemp's finishing ability, and Gibson's power-hitting providing encouraging signs. Team form (Last 5 completed T20Is, recent first) - IND-W - LLWLW | ENG-W - WWLWL. What to expect? This is a warm-up match, and the result will be forgotten the moment the World Cup begins. But what happens on the field at Sophia Gardens will linger in the minds of both team managements. For India, this is about finalizing the middle-order puzzle - does Bharti Fulmali walk into the XI for the tournament opener against Pakistan? For England, it's about regaining confidence after a loss to Australia and ensuring their new-look top order finds stability before their campaign begins against Sri Lanka.
